# BAD-093 — refreshCollab's supersession guard silently cancels the arrival pull, and nobody retries it

## Brief
BAD-090 kept the sync's pull out from under this guard, but refreshCollab(pack, {pull:true}) still runs its own pull below it, and that path is how a scene ARRIVES in a room. onSceneSelected/selectPack fires it un-awaited; if the 20s focus poll, openCollabModal, a seat claim or a collab:changed event bumps collab.seq in the window between the read and the pull, the arrival pull is abandoned with no retry and no error, and the superseding refresh passes pull:false so it fetches nothing. The person who just opened a collab scene sees an empty room for up to 60s. autoPullWrapped is worse: it is once per room per run (collabAutoPulled guards it), so its single pull being superseded means the wrapped room's takes wait on the poll with no second attempt. The fix is probably to say in refreshCollab what BAD-090 said in runCollabSync — supersession cancels the PAINT, not the TRANSFER — by running the pull before the seq check and gating only the toast and the renders on it. That needs web/collabweb-model.js, which was outside BAD-090's deliverables.

Evidence: web/collabweb-model.js:203 is the guard ('if (seq !== collab.seq || ...) return false;'), :224-228 is the pull branch below it. renderer/app.js:4759 and :4786-4790 are the same pair. Callers that bump the seq without pulling: web/collabweb.js:136 (20s focus poll), web/collabweb-modal.js:69, web/collabweb-tab.js:213, web/collabweb-seat.js:60/87/101, renderer/app.js:4876 (focus poll) and :4897. BAD-090's test/collabreads.test.js reproduces the identical mechanism for the sync path ('a focus poll landing mid-cycle does not cancel the cycle`s pull') — that test fails on the folded version with wire 'upload-url -> commit -> info -> info' and an empty remote store. Found by BADS-090/Desiree.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, WEB ONLY (Eric, 2026-09-16): a correctness fix to concurrent code, small in lines and expensive if wrong. renderer/app.js is deferred-desktop and out of scope; the identical fix is recorded on BAD-041 as a follow-up PR owed right after the collab part of renderer/app.js is extracted, deliberately not folded into a move PR because BAD-036's pure-move rule governs that ticket. The engineer spawns its own reviewer, the shape BAD-090 used, because BAD-090's first cut was blocked by exactly that reviewer for exactly this class of mistake.
